back: A record for each material of quantities and values received, issued and held, used to cost issues to jobs.
Reorder level - (average usage × average lead time).
Reorder level + reorder quantity - (minimum usage × minimum lead time).
The oldest stock is issued first, so one issue may use two or more prices; the closing stock is valued at the latest prices.
Gross wages = basic pay + overtime. Net wages = gross wages - tax and pension deductions.
Idle time and, usually, the overtime premium are treated as production overheads, not direct labour.
Materials arrive when needed and goods are made to order, so stock is kept very low.
Benefits: lower storage costs, less cash tied up, less waste. Risks: late deliveries stop production; no bulk discounts; reliance on suppliers.
